log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 56% BRING: dragapult, 30% BRING: garchomp, 5% BRING: gholdengo
Pick 2: 73% BRING: garchomp, 19% BRING: gholdengo, 4% BRING: greninja
Pick 3: 81% BRING: gholdengo, 11% BRING: scizor, 7% BRING: greninja

Opponent is faster with Dragapult and Greninja and physical with Palafin and Garchomp, so Intimidate control is the deciding factor. Incineroar leads for Fake Out and Parting Shot, Primarina walls Palafin and knocks out dragons, and Multiscale Dragonite revenges with priority and Ice Punch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating speed, knockout potential, and matchup to select the single best legal action under the Pokémon Champions format constraints.Parsing the team preview to choose the initial three Pokémon and lead order for the battle.Evaluating type matchups and mega constraints to select the three-Pokémon lineup and lead.

decisions.thought: 34% MOVE: suckerpunch, 21% SWITCH: garchomp, 18% MOVE: shadowball
Incineroar is slower than Dragapult and in a bad matchup with no strong hit. Parting Shot lowers its offenses and pivots to a better answer.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating turn decision constraints for Pokémon Champions singles format and action selection.Assessing priority and type matchup constraints to choose between switching and attacking.Evaluating type immunities and pivot options to select the safest switch-in.

decisions.thought: We must switch after Parting Shot. Preserving Dragonite's Multiscale is the deciding factor, so avoid a bad matchup into a possibly Dragon move. Primarina's Fairy immunity walls Dragon STAB and tanks weakened Ghost hits.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating speed, knockout potential, and matchup to select the single best legal action.Assessing remaining opponent options and hazard state to confirm the switch choice.Evaluating Primarina versus Dragonite switch matchups against the revealed Dragapult and remaining team threats.

decisions.thought: 46% SWITCH: garchomp, 41% MOVE: suckerpunch, 13% SWITCH: gholdengo

Primarina is a good matchup here since it resists Dark and is immune to Dragon despite moving second. Dragapult is weakened to -2 Attack and -1 SpA, so it cannot threaten much. Moonblast is super effective and threatens a knockout.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing turn constraints and selecting the single best legal action based on speed, knockout potential, or matchup.Evaluating remaining opponent options and turn-two move choice against a weakened Dragapult.Selecting Moonblast as the highest-damage option against the debuffed Dragapult while accounting for speed and type matchup.

decisions.thought: 40% MOVE: shadowball, 24% SWITCH: gholdengo, 19% MOVE: suckerpunch

Dragapult moves first on speed, but Primarina is immune to Dragon and bulky enough to survive one Ghost or Electric hit.
Moonblast is super effective and should be a likely knockout on frail Dragapult.
Switching out wastes a free KO, so stay and attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating turn decision rules and action format constraints for Pokémon Champions singles.Assessing move and switch options against a faster Dragapult with unknown ability and item.Evaluating Primarina's Moonblast KO chance versus Dragapult's Thunderbolt risk and Incineroar's Ghost resistance.Assessing physical Dragapult's Phantom Force threat and switching to Incineroar for Ghost resistance and Intimidate.

decisions.thought: 82% MOVE: shadowball, 10% MOVE: recover, 4% MOVE: flashcannon
Primarina is in a bad matchup: Moonblast is resisted and Gholdengo is faster. Staying risks losing Primarina for little damage. Switching to Incineroar resists its Steel/Ghost STABs.

decisions.thought: 69% MOVE: shadowball, 17% MOVE: recover, 8% MOVE: ironhead
Gholdengo outspeeds but its Shadow Ball is resisted, so Incineroar wins the trade. Parting Shot and Taunt fail into Good as Gold, while Flare Blitz is super effective and threatens a knockout.
